basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 20.' and it opens 'Vers. 20. Videbantur pauci dies. Quare dicit: Videbantur pauci dies, cum amatori etiam'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 20. Videbantur pauci dies. Quare dicit: Videbantur pauci dies, cum amatori etiam breve tempus longe videatur? Sed hoc dicit propter servitutem, quae licet dura esset, facilis ei videbatur propter amoris magnitudinem.
